solutions.check: grid and clues read from the Guardian's printable copy, its numbering matching the numbers printed in it and the clue list; every fifteensquared answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Modernization rendering one strangely agog about international decoration

indicators.note: about says the scrambled letters go around the remaining pieces, enclosing them
strangely says the letters of the word agog are rearranged in an odd new order

parts.note: an ornament is a decoration

explanation.surface: Someone finds a modern makeover makes them oddly excited about a decoration from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendering one' just links the definition to the wordplay; 'about' has the scrambled letters enclose the international decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian loanword names the bringing up to date of an institution, originally the Catholic Church after Vatican II.

clue.text: Walter's wench regarding cheesy pastry

parts.note: gouge is a Scots word for a wench, marked in Chambers as used by Sir Walter Scott
re means regarding or concerning

explanation.surface: A Scott heroine is somehow connected with a cheese-flavoured bake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walter' is Sir Walter Scott, the Scottish novelist; Chambers tags words found only in his writing as Scott's.
explanation.definitionFit: A choux pastry ball flavoured with cheese, from Burgundy, is the French savoury puff so named.

clue.text: Advertisement boosted big mouthful

indicators.note: in a down clue, boosted means lifted upward, so the word is read from the bottom up

parts.note: a plug is a piece of publicity, an advertisement

explanation.surface: An advert that has been heavily promoted leaves someone with a lot to swallow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boosted' pushes PLUG upward in this down entry, so it is read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A large swallow of drink or food taken in one go is a common noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Enteric region, part of mobile umbles

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Offal that moves about includes a section of the gut.
explanation.definitionFit: Enteric means of the intestines; this is the last section of the small intestine.

clue.text: Part of spurge family I see among crumbling ruins

indicators.note: among says the next pieces sit inside the rearranged letters
crumbling ruins fall apart, so the letters of ruins are scattered into a new order

parts.note: the letter C is pronounced see, a standard crossword equivalence

explanation.surface: Someone spots a plant growing amid tumbledown ruins.
explanation.walkthrough: RUINS rearranged gives RINUS, and IC goes in after the R.
explanation.definitionFit: This genus, containing the castor-oil plant, belongs to the spurge family, Euphorbiaceae.

clue.text: It may attract bees, i.e. with garden cut roughly

indicators.note: roughly says the letters are put together only approximately, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gardener muses that a roughly trimmed garden still draws bees.
explanation.walkthrough: Chambers hyphenates the term as NECTAR-GUIDE, though the enumeration gives it as one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A marking on a petal that guides pollinating insects towards the nectar is the botanical term for this.

clue.text: Shopping centre making money without limit

parts.note: M is an abbreviation for money given in Chambers
all, as in everything, has no limit

explanation.surface: A shopping complex rakes in cash endlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A large enclosed complex of shops is a common North American term now used everywhere.

clue.text: Pacific island country and what surrounds it — it's sickening

parts.note: NAU is the international vehicle registration code for Nauru, a Pacific island state
an island is surrounded by sea

explanation.surface: A tiny Pacific nation and its ocean prompt a queasy remark.
explanation.walkthrough: NAU is Nauru's car code, an obscure abbreviation; Nauru is a small island republic in the Pacific.
explanation.definitionFit: Sickness of the stomach, the feeling of wanting to vomit, is what sickening things produce.

clue.text: Early festival, restrained by the sound of it

indicators.note: by the sound of it says a word with the same pronunciation is wanted

parts.note: tied means restrained, as with rope

explanation.surface: An ancient celebration was apparently kept in check.
explanation.definitionFit: The old sense of a season or feast day survives in compounds such as Yuletide and Whitsuntide.

clue.text: Upper-class in strange reversion to cover unduly

indicators.note: in says the posh letter goes inside the rearranged word
strange says the letters of reversion are put in an unfamiliar order

explanation.surface: A posh person's odd reversal of policy leads to excessive protection.
explanation.walkthrough: REVERSION rearranged around U gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking out a policy for more than the value at risk is protecting something excessively.

clue.text: Old serviceman, in essence reverse of free but filled with energy

parts.note: the soul is the essence of a thing

indicators.note: filled with says the next letter goes inside the reversed word
reverse of says the following word is read backwards

parts.note: to rid is to free
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: An old soldier is, at heart, the opposite of free but full of vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: RID reversed is DIR, which takes E inside to make DIER.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an obsolete spelling of a word for a member of an army, found in older texts.

clue.text: Pair of notes of different lengths to frustrate easy task (10, two words)

definitions.text: Pair of notes of different lengths

parts.note: to scotch a plan is to frustrate it
a snap is something easily done

explanation.surface: A musical phrase seems to thwart a simple job.
explanation.walkthrough: In music this is a short accented note followed by a longer one, typical of Scottish reels and strathspeys.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhythm of a short stressed note before a longer one is the musical figure meant.

clue.text: A bit of Scotch, giving one good boost

parts.note: a lift is a boost

explanation.surface: A dram of whisky gives someone a welcome pick-me-up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of Scotch' marks a Scots word, not whisky; Chambers gives it as an obsolete Scots term for a moment or glimpse.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scots dialect noun means a brief moment, a little while, so a short space of time.

clue.text: Copper with support of law trailing bloodscker

indicators.note: trailing says the word for law comes after the copper symbol

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
lex is Latin for law, used in English legal phrases

explanation.surface: A policeman, backed by the law, pursues a bloodsucker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bloodscker' is the printed typo for bloodsucker; 'with support of' only links the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: This genus contains the common gnat or house mosquito, whose females feed on blood.

clue.text: Hint, reverse of banal, splitting outsiders in audience

indicators.note: splitting says the reversed word goes between the two outer letters, parting them
outsiders in says take only the first and last letters of the next word
reverse of says the word for banal is read backwards

parts.note: dull means banal or uninteresting

explanation.surface: A hint of the mundane is spoken among those at the edges of a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'audience' supplies only its outside letters, which the turned-round banal word splits apart.
explanation.definitionFit: To refer indirectly or suggestively to something is to hint at it.

clue.text: Stimulant that could make one live, astir

indicators.note: could make says these letters can be formed into another word

explanation.surface: A tonic is something that would make you lively and active.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that gives vigour or life is a stimulant, from vitalise meaning to invigorate.

clue.text: Forewings become reversed on Asiatic bird

indicators.note: reversed says the word for become is read backwards

parts.note: to get, as in get tired, is to become
the mina, also spelt myna, is an Asian starling

explanation.surface: A bird from Asia turns its wings around.
explanation.walkthrough: GET reversed gives TEG, followed by MINA.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the hardened front wings of insects such as grasshoppers and cockroaches, the plural of tegmen.

clue.text: Peter keeping folio in cover?

indicators.note: keeping says the envelope holds the next letter inside it

parts.note: an SAE, stamped addressed envelope, is a cover for a letter

explanation.surface: A man named Peter keeps a sheet of paper inside a folder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peter' is not a name but criminal slang for a safe; SAE is a stamped addressed envelope.
explanation.definitionFit: In old criminal slang a peter is a strongbox, hence a peterman was a safe-breaker.

clue.text: Mantras concealed in Bowie hit

indicators.note: concealed says the letters of mantras are disguised by rearrangement

explanation.surface: Hidden chants lurk inside a David Bowie single.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealed in' tempts a search for hidden letters, but the answer is MANTRAS rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1972 single by David Bowie, about a space visitor, was one of his best-known songs.

clue.text: Such as Brown Bess, girl tucking into strong drinks

indicators.note: tucking into says the girl goes inside the drinks

parts.note: gins are strong spirits
gal is an informal word for girl

explanation.surface: A girl is getting stuck into some spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: Brown Bess was the British army's musket; gingals are heavy muskets used in India and China, so 'such as' is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: These heavy swivel-mounted muskets are classed with old firearms like the famous British Brown Bess.

clue.text: He's freed from road accidents, insensitive

indicators.note: freed from says the two letters are released from the longer word

parts.note: crashes are road accidents
he is taken as written, its two letters

explanation.surface: A man escapes from some car crashes, callous though it seems.
explanation.walkthrough: CRASHES loses HE.
explanation.definitionFit: Grossly stupid or unfeeling, lacking delicacy, is what this word describes.

clue.text: Container in chemistry lab due to crack when filling completely

indicators.note: filling says the rearranged letters go inside the word for completely

parts.note: all means completely, as in all alone

indicators.note: to crack says the letters of due break apart into a new order

explanation.surface: A lab experiment is due to crack when the vessel is full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is only a link; 'lab' belongs to the definition, though it looks like anagram fodder beside 'due'.
explanation.definitionFit: This pear-shaped earthenware vessel was used in old chemistry for sublimation.

clue.text: Trooper former monarch despatched, making money abroad

indicators.note: despatched says the monarch is sent away, removed from the word

parts.note: a trooper is a soldier
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the cipher of the late Queen, a former monarch

explanation.surface: A soldier kills an ex-king and makes a fortune overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: SOLDIER loses ER, the royal cipher of Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: These are Italian coins, the plural of soldo, an old copper coin.

clue.text: Spot, in short, is endless contamination

parts.note: is shortened is the 's of it's, a lone S

indicators.note: endless says the final letter is dropped

parts.note: a taint is a contamination

explanation.surface: A mark, put briefly, is a contamination that never ends.
explanation.walkthrough: TAINT loses its last T.
explanation.definitionFit: A discoloured mark or blemish on cloth or skin is a spot.

clue.text: Reputation once made in battle

definitions.meaning: an obsolete word for praise or renown, from Latin laus
the 1915 Battle of ..., a British offensive on the Western Front in France

explanation.definitionFit: The obsolete noun meant fame or praise, and the French mining town gave its name to a First World War battle.

clue.text: Waiters chatter about recipe to scan

indicators.note: about says the chatter goes around the other pieces

parts.note: gas is idle chatter
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, on prescriptions
to con is to study or scan

explanation.surface: Restaurant staff gossip over a recipe to look it over.
explanation.walkthrough: GAS goes round R plus CON. R is the prescription abbreviation for Latin recipe, take.
explanation.definitionFit: French for boys, the word is used for waiters in French restaurants and cafes.

clue.text: Group of fellow graduates displaying quality

definitions.meaning: the year group that graduated together

explanation.definitionFit: The noun covers both a cohort of students and, informally, distinction or style.

clue.text: Piece of art, cup fashioned with lustre

indicators.note: fashioned says the letters are shaped into a new form

explanation.surface: A trophy is crafted to have a shine.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-dimensional work such as a statue or carving is a piece of art.

clue.text: College harem, wherewith story ends?

parts.note: an oda is a room in a harem

explanation.surface: A tale of a college harem concludes with a twist.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is musical by origin; 'story' widens it to a closing section of anything.
explanation.definitionFit: A concluding passage that rounds off a piece of music or a narrative is a tailpiece.

clue.text: Alternate bits of sphere on heraldic fur

indicators.note: alternate bits of says take every other letter of the following words

explanation.surface: Every other piece of a globe sits on a coat of arms.
explanation.walkthrough: The picks are the 2nd, 4th, 6th and 8th letters of 'sphere on'. Blog commenters note that Chambers spells the heraldic fur PEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: The setter's spelling names the heraldic fur that is black with gold spots, the reverse of erminois.

clue.text: Siamese twins in three pairs?

annotationWithheld.why: Siamese twins in three pairs? (4): THAI = TH from 'three' and AI from 'pairs', but no single selection device picks those two-letter runs, and blog commenters question how the 'twins' are identified.

clue.text: One about to drop off? I may be in agreement

definitions.meaning: someone nodding off, about to fall asleep
one who nods the head to show assent

explanation.definitionFit: The noun names both a drowsy person whose head droops and someone who signals assent by moving the head.

clue.text: Flow of mud? How surprising when it splits both sides

indicators.note: splits says the exclamation goes between the two side letters, parting them

parts.note: L and R stand for left and right, both sides
aha is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A mudslide astonishes everyone when it parts on both sides.
explanation.walkthrough: AHA goes between L and R, left and right.
explanation.definitionFit: A volcanic mudflow of ash and water racing down a slope is the geological term.

clue.text: Scottish millstream on the market? This'll be included (8, three words, apostrophe)

parts.note: a dam in Scots is a millstream or mill race, so a Scottish millstream is a dam
something on the market is for sale

explanation.surface: A Highland mill race is up for sale, with the water thrown in.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition sits at the end: water is what a millstream contains, and this humorous name for it is the answer. Chambers spells it as two words, though three are given.
explanation.definitionFit: This jocular name for water says it was the only drink of the first man.

clue.text: One favouring recreation? Fencing is tense in a way

parts.note: paling is fencing made of stakes

indicators.note: in a way says the letters of is tense are arranged in another way

explanation.surface: A fencing enthusiast is tense in some fashion, keen on leisure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recreation' is re-creation: a believer in rebirth or regeneration.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who holds the doctrine of rebirth or regeneration believes in being created anew.
